applicant_utility.summary: This is a funded secondment, not a studentship: twelve researchers are placed at Dutch missions (from Canberra to Hanoi) for one to three months to feed scientific expertise into Dutch foreign policy, funded up to EUR 30,000 including a replacement grant that pays your institution back for your absence. The decisive factor is mission fit: forty percent of the score is the match between you and the mission's own project description, so read the Call for Proposals annexes before choosing a position. Remember the presentation rules: the narrative CV is capped at 500 words, key outputs at five items, and any mention of h-indexes or journal impact factors is prohibited.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Employed researchers at a Dutch knowledge institution whose expertise matches a specific mission's project and who can be released for one to three months before 29 February 2028.

applicant_utility.summary: KITLV pays the practicalities of a three-month research stay in Leiden: your return fare, accommodation up to EUR 2,000 a month against receipts, local transport, an office, and a case-by-case top-up for higher Leiden living costs, but it is explicitly not a salary, so you must arrive with a steady income. Unusually, you need no university affiliation to apply; a self-directed publication or research project in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies is the actual ticket. Selection is documents-only with no interviews, which means your two-page CV and project proposal are the whole competition.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Independent or affiliated postdocs with a PhD in the humanities or social sciences whose Southeast Asian or Caribbean project benefits from KITLV's collections and who can self-fund base living costs.
